outputs.L1: A memory device includes: a plurality of bank groups, each comprising one or more banks; a first bus coupled to the plurality of bank groups; a second bus coupled to the plurality of bank groups; a toggle signal generation unit configured to generate a first signal that toggles in response to a column command signal and a second signal having a logic value opposite to that of the first signal; a column command transmission unit configured to transmit a read command signal or a write command signal to the first bus when the first signal is activated and to the second bus when the second signal is activated; and a column address transmission unit configured to transmit one or more column address signals corresponding to the read command signal or the write command signal to whichever of the first and second buses carries the read command signal or the write command signal.
outputs.L3:
The memory device includes a plurality of bank groups, with each bank group comprising one or more memory banks. A first bus and a second bus are coupled to the plurality of bank groups to support the transmission of commands and addresses.

The memory device further includes a toggle-signal generation unit configured to generate a first toggle signal in response to a column command signal. The unit also generates a second toggle signal having a logic value opposite to that of the first toggle signal. Accordingly, when one toggle signal is activated, the other toggle signal is deactivated.

A column-command transmission unit uses the first and second toggle signals to select between the two buses. More specifically, the transmission unit alternately sends a read command signal or a write command signal through either the first bus or the second bus, depending on which toggle signal is activated. A column-address transmission unit similarly transmits the column address associated with the read or write command. The column address is sent through the same bus selected for carrying the corresponding command signal, thereby maintaining alignment between each column command and its associated address.
outputs.L4:
A memory device includes a plurality of memory bank groups that share first and second buses for receiving read or write commands and associated column addresses. A transmission circuit is coupled between a command-and-address input path and the two buses. The transmission circuit includes toggle-controlled transmission units configured to select one of the buses for each incoming command. When a read or write command is received, the corresponding column address is transferred through the same transmission unit and onto the same selected bus as the command.

The toggle control changes state in response to successive read or write operations. In a first state, a command and its column address are transmitted over the first bus, while the second bus remains available for another transfer. In a second state, the next command and its column address are transmitted over the second bus. The transmission units therefore alternate the command-and-address pairs between the two shared buses.

Each bank group is coupled to the buses and accepts the command and column address carried by the bus selected for that operation. Because a command and its associated address always travel together on one bus, the device preserves their correspondence and avoids routing the command and address through different signal paths. Alternating successive operations between the buses also organizes command distribution, reduces contention on a single bus, and supports efficient access to the multiple memory banks.
outputs.L5:
### A Memory Device

A memory device is a piece of hardware used to store digital information. Computers, smartphones, cameras, and many other electronic devices rely on memory devices to save files, applications, photographs, and system data. Common examples include hard disk drives, solid-state drives, USB flash drives, memory cards, and optical discs.

Memory devices may provide temporary or permanent storage. Random-access memory, or RAM, stores information only while a device is operating, allowing programs to run quickly. By contrast, drives and memory cards keep data even when the power is turned off. The capacity of a memory device is usually measured in gigabytes or terabytes.

Modern memory devices have become smaller, faster, and more reliable. However, they can still be damaged or lost, so important information should be backed up regularly. As technology continues to develop, memory devices will remain essential for storing and accessing the growing amount of digital data in everyday life.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style apparatus claim for a memory device that alternates read/write column commands and corresponding column addresses between two buses coupled to multiple bank groups using complementary toggle signals.
counterfactuals.output:
1. **A memory device comprising:**

a plurality of bank groups, each bank group comprising at least one memory bank;

a first column-command-and-address bus and a second column-command-and-address bus, each coupled to the plurality of bank groups; and

control circuitry configured to:

- generate a first toggle signal and a second toggle signal complementary to the first toggle signal;
- receive a sequence of column operations, each column operation comprising a read or write column command and a corresponding column address; and
- alternately provide successive column operations of the sequence on the first and second column-command-and-address buses responsive to the first and second toggle signals, respectively, such that the read or write column command and the corresponding column address of each column operation are provided on a same one of the first and second column-command-and-address buses for access to a selected bank group of the plurality of bank groups.
